title: Finite stratified restrictions detect pro-etale sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $(i_\alpha:X_\alpha\to X)_\alpha$ be a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification]. On each $X_\alpha$ choose a pro-etale covering $(v_{\alpha j}:V_{\alpha j}\to X_\alpha)_j$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For every abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, if $v_{\alpha j}^{-1}i_\alpha^{-1}F=0$ for all $\alpha,j$, then $F=0$, where inverse images are [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. In particular, for any ring sheaf $R$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the termwise exact inverse images to modules over its inverse images jointly detect zero objects and isomorphisms in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open), and Tag 09AB (lemma-thickening), followed by Noetherian induction. The induction and covering detection are agent consequences, not the literal statements of those lemmas.

proof.text: First record composition of restrictions, including along the open subschemes used below. For composable scheme maps $a,b$, the direct-image formula identifies $a_*b_*$ with $(ab)_*$: on an object $W$ the two sections are evaluated on $(W\times X_a)\times X_b\cong W\times X_b$. Composing the two adjunction bijections therefore identifies $b^{-1}a^{-1}$ with $(ab)^{-1}$, naturally in the sheaf. This is the uniqueness of a representing object for the same Hom functor, and also identifies restriction along an identity with the identity. In particular restrictions of a sheaf already zero on a stratum remain zero after any further restriction.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-functoriality; composition by the displayed direct-image formula and adjunction

proof.text: For any scheme $T$, let $(v_j:V_j\to T)_j$ be a pro-etale covering and $G$ an abelian sheaf whose inverse images on the $V_j$ vanish. Regard an abelian sheaf as a module over the constant integer sheaf: integers act by repeated addition, with locally constant integers acting locally and gluing. The localization theorem identifies $v_j^{-1}G$ with slice restriction, so for any object $W\to T$, the restriction of every $s\in G(W)$ to $W\times_TV_j$ is zero. These fibre products cover $W$ by the covering axiom. Separatedness in the sheaf axiom gives $s=0$. Hence $G=0$. Apply this with $G=i_\alpha^{-1}F$ to remove the chosen coverings from the hypothesis. The same argument will glue vanishing over an open covering of $X$.

source.place: Tag 09A5 and localization at objects; covering and sheaf axioms; integer action is repeated addition

proof.text: Prove by induction on $n$ that restrictions to any stratification with at most $n$ strata detect zero abelian sheaves on every Noetherian scheme. For $n=0$ the scheme is empty, and the empty covering forces every sheaf of abelian groups to have zero sections. For the induction step discard empty strata. For each remaining $i_\alpha:X_\alpha\to X$, the definition of immersion gives a factorization $X_\alpha\hookrightarrow W_\alpha\hookrightarrow X$, closed followed by open. The opens $W_\alpha$ cover $X$ because their images contain the strata. Write $Z_\alpha=X_\alpha$, viewed with this actual closed-immersion structure in $W_\alpha$, and put $U_\alpha=W_\alpha\setminus |Z_\alpha|$. Both $W_\alpha$ and $U_\alpha$ are Noetherian by open-subscheme permanence. Moreover $U_\alpha\to W_\alpha$ is quasi-compact: for any affine open $B\subset W_\alpha$, the open $B\cap U_\alpha$ of the Noetherian scheme $X$ is quasi-compact by that same permanence theorem. This checks the morphism hypothesis, not just quasi-compactness of $U_\alpha$ itself.

source.place: Tags 01OW (lemma-locally-Noetherian), 01OZ (lemma-Noetherian-topology); induction using the immersion factorization

proof.text: On $U_\alpha$ base-change the original stratification. Its $\alpha$-stratum is empty, so discard it; the other strata form a stratification with at most $n-1$ strata. The pullback-stratification lemma supplies the schemes and immersions, not merely a partition of points. By step 1, the restriction $F|_{U_\alpha}$ has zero restriction to each of them, since every original $i_\beta^{-1}F$ is zero by step 2. The induction hypothesis applied to the Noetherian scheme $U_\alpha$ gives $F|_{U_\alpha}=0$. Also the closed restriction of $F|_{W_\alpha}$ to $Z_\alpha=X_\alpha$ is zero by step 1. Apply open/closed detection to $F|_{W_\alpha}$, regarded as a module sheaf over the constant integer sheaf as in step 2. Its two inverse images vanish and its open complement is quasi-compact by step 3, so $F|_{W_\alpha}=0$. The open-cover case of step 2 now gives $F=0$, completing the induction. At no point is an arbitrary subscheme replaced by its reduced structure.

source.place: Tag 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open), in its zero-object consequence lem-exc-open-closed-detection; finite-stratum induction is an agent argument

proof.text: Let now $R$ be any ring sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. For a scheme map $u$, inverse image takes an $R$-module sheaf to a module over $u^{-1}R$ by applying inverse image to its addition and action. There is no scalar extension to a different coefficient ring here. Underlying abelian inverse image is exact by the site-pullback theorem. Kernels and cokernels of module sheaves have the underlying abelian kernels and cokernels, so this module functor is exact. The exact-functor theorem induces its termwise triangulated functor on the unbounded derived categories. Explicitly, preservation of kernels and cokernels gives $u^{-1}H^q(K)=H^q(u^{-1}K)$: the cohomology quotient is the cokernel of the image of the previous differential in the next kernel. The sheaf result of steps 1--4 applies to underlying abelian sheaves, hence detects zero $R$-modules as well.

source.place: Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact), first assertion; Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian); derived.tex Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor)

proof.text: If a derived object $K$ restricts to zero on every chosen covering of every stratum, step 5 gives zero restrictions of $H^q(K)$ for every integer $q$. The abelian-sheaf result makes $H^q(K)=0$ for all $q$. Choose a representing complex $C$; the map $0\to C$ is then a quasi-isomorphism, so its image in the localization is an isomorphism $0\cong K$. Conversely an additive restriction functor sends a zero object to zero. This proves joint zero detection without boundedness assumptions.

For a morphism $f:K\to L$ in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$, complete it to a distinguished triangle $K\xrightarrow f L\to C\to K[1]$. Each restriction is triangulated by step 5. If every restricted $f$ is invertible, the long exact cohomology sequence of each restricted triangle makes every cohomology object of the restricted $C$ zero; the localization argument in step 6 makes that restricted cone zero. Joint zero detection gives $C=0$. Apply Hom$(W,-)$ exactness to the global triangle and its rotations: since both $C$ and $C[-1]$ are zero, Hom$(W,f)$ is bijective for every $W$. Taking $W=L$ gives $h:L\to K$ with $fh=1_L$; injectivity for $W=K$ applied to $hf$ and $1_K$ gives $hf=1_K$. Thus $f$ is invertible. The converse follows since every functor preserves isomorphisms.
